findings.description: TF-020H3-003 closure description in STATUS.md names 'Both occurrences fixed' but the TF filing (020H.3 R1 completeness COMP-MIN-003 + 020F COMP-004) and the DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criterion (viii) state there are THREE corrections: (1) §4 020F `extends:` shorthand trailing dash, (2) §4 020H part 3 Renovate marker comment trailing dash, and (3) §4 020H part 3 `uses:` line trailing dash. The diff confirms all three are made in the plan file. However, the STATUS.md TF-020H3-003 closure entry reads 'Both occurrences fixed' rather than naming all three. An auditor reading cold sees 'both' but the TF filing says two places and the plan has three corrected lines. The actual closure description is ambiguous — it mentions 'Both occurrences fixed: §4 020F ... AND §4 020H part 3 ... `# renovate:` ... + `uses:` ...' which is the right enumeration but the leading 'Both' is misleading (there are three corrected lines across two logical locations). This is a documentation precision gap that could cause a future auditor to question whether the closure was complete.
findings.recommendation: Update the TF-020H3-003 STATUS.md closure entry from 'Both occurrences fixed' to 'Three lines corrected across two locations fixed' or rephrase to clearly enumerate the three line corrections (§4 020F extends shorthand, §4 020H part 3 renovate marker comment, §4 020H part 3 uses line) so the count matches the TF's stated scope ('two places' in the TF description, three corrected lines in practice).
findings.rationale: The TF was filed as covering 'BOTH workflows: policy-check.yml + release-gate.yml' for TF-020H3rg-002, and 'two places' for TF-020H3-003. A closure description that says 'Both' when three lines were changed will trigger audit questions in 6 months. Completeness governance requires closure descriptions to be unambiguous against the original TF scope.

findings.description: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 'Supply-chain posture' describes the workflow's supply-chain as covering OPA, Conftest, and Regal binary SHA256 verification, but does NOT mention the new Python dependency hash-pinning introduced by slice 020M. An adopter reading §12.7.13 before deploying gets a materially incomplete picture of the v1.0.1 supply-chain posture — they will see the binary-SHA256 posture described but not know that Python deps (pyyaml, jsonschema, attrs, referencing, rpds-py, jsonschema-specifications) are now also hash-pinned via requirements/policy-check.txt. The v1.0.1 release notes correctly describe the change and the DISPATCH-NOTE (viii) invokes this as acceptance criterion, but the canonical adopter reference (ADOPT-001 §12.7.13) is not updated. This creates a stale supply-chain disclosure against the v1.0.1 tag.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Python dependency hash-pinning (post-020M / v1.0.1)' sub-section to ADOPT-001 §12.7.13. At minimum, one sentence: 'From v1.0.1, Python dependencies (pyyaml, jsonschema, and their transitive closure) are installed with `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements/policy-check.txt`, generated by `pip-compile --generate-hashes`. A PyPI-served wheel whose SHA256 is not in the lockfile causes pip to refuse the install.' Alternatively, file a tracked-forward item (new TF) as a v1.1 ADOPT-001 maintenance task, since 020M is a PATCH bump and §12.7.13 is a disclosure section, not a behaviour-change section. Either path closes the gap; the TF path is acceptable at PATCH if filed in STATUS.md.
findings.rationale: §12.7.13 is the canonical supply-chain disclosure document adopters read 'before deploying'. Shipping v1.0.1 with an updated supply-chain posture that is not reflected in the primary adopter reference is a disclosure gap. Per the review package examination item (9), the lens must check whether §12.7 wording is stale relative to this slice and file a TF if refresh is needed.

findings.description: ADOPT-001 §12.7.4 (break-glass procedure) still contains the sentence 'release-tag-time refusal of expired entries is tracked as TF-005 (deferred — adds to 020D2 / a future release-cut workflow).' TF-005 was closed in slice 020H.3. This parenthetical cross-reference now points to a closed TF and a mechanism that has been delivered, making the sentence technically stale. The sentence body ('The runtime warning IS shipped at v1.0.0') remains accurate but the TF-005 deferral note no longer reflects current state.
findings.recommendation: Update the §12.7.4 sentence to reflect that TF-005 is closed: remove the '(deferred — adds to 020D2 / a future release-cut workflow)' parenthetical and replace with a forward-reference to §12.7.7's SCP-EREL-001 entry, or simply state 'release-tag-time refusal of expired entries is enforced by the release-gate workflow (`.github/workflows/release-gate.yml`) per slice 020H.3.' This is a v1.1 maintenance pass item; file as a new TF if not addressed in this slice.
findings.rationale: The TF-005 deferral note in §12.7.4 was accurate at v1.0.0 but is now stale documentation. An adopter reading it cold would incorrectly believe that release-tag-time enforcement is not yet available. At a PATCH bump this is not blocking, but it is a documentation accuracy gap that should be tracked.

findings.description: The 'How adopters can verify' section of v1.0.1.md correctly documents the happy path but does not document the case where the conditional `if ! python3 -c 'import yaml'` skip IS taken (runner already has pyyaml preinstalled). The release notes state 'If a runner already has pyyaml / jsonschema importable... the conditional skip is taken, no install runs, and no hash check happens — same green-path behaviour as v1.0.0.' This is accurate, but an adopter who wants to verify that the hash-pinning is actually exercising may be left without guidance on how to test or observe that code path. The DISPATCH-NOTE §Risk surface item 1 notes the same thing but the release notes do not link to it or acknowledge the observability gap.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to the 'How adopters can verify' section: 'To verify the hash-pinned install path is exercised on your runner (rather than the preinstalled-package skip), check the step run-log — the skip path emits no install output; the hash-pin path emits `pip install --require-hashes` output. If your runner environment always has these packages preinstalled, the hash verification is a no-op; consider a fresh runner environment test if supply-chain auditability of this specific step is required.' This is non-blocking at ship.
findings.rationale: The release notes are the primary adopter-facing document for v1.0.1 changes. An adopter whose runner preinstalls pyyaml/jsonschema will never exercise the --require-hashes path. For supply-chain audit purposes, this is an observability gap worth disclosing in the release notes, even if the security posture is equivalent.

The TF appears once at STATUS.md line 142 (in the 'Tracked-forward items from 020H.3 (release-gate)' section with full detail) and again at line 179 (in the Post-Threshold-A backlog section, abbreviated). Having both is fine for navigation but creates two closure records for the same TF.
findings.recommendation: Cosmetic only — the duplicate entry is acceptable. If cleaning up, the backlog entry (line ~179) can be removed since the authoritative closure is in the tracked-forward section (line ~142). No action required for merge.
findings.rationale: Cosmetic duplication; both entries are accurate. Does not affect auditor ability to understand slice state.

findings.description: Post-Threshold-A backlog section does not yet have 020M listed as a ✅ landed entry (correctly, since this is IN FLIGHT). The DISPATCH-NOTE and review package acknowledge this is a close-out action. The close-out plan (post-merge steps (x) and (xi) in the DISPATCH-NOTE) covers the memory update requirement. Verifying the close-out task list captures memory updates for project_wp_scp_022_plan.md and project_post_threshold_a_state.md: the DISPATCH-NOTE's post-merge items (x) and (xi) cover the tag-cut but do not explicitly name the memory files. This is a documentation gap in the close-out plan.
findings.recommendation: The operator's close-out actions for 020M should explicitly include: (1) flipping the STATUS.md 020M entry from IN FLIGHT to ✅ landed with PR number and commit SHA, (2) updating project_post_threshold_a_state.md in auto-memory to add 020M to the landed slices list, (3) updating project_wp_scp_022_plan.md in auto-memory to reflect 020M closure. Consider adding a note to the DISPATCH-NOTE's close-out checklist. Non-blocking at merge.
findings.rationale: The review package examination item (14) specifically requires verifying the close-out task list captures memory entries. The DISPATCH-NOTE does not enumerate these memory files, creating a risk that the operator forgets the memory update after merge.

findings.description: The renovate/default.json preset does not need updating for v1.0.1 (PATCH bump, no renovate/v* tag bump needed). The preset continues to bump SCP wrapper SHAs across the estate. The `requirements/**` path is NOT covered in the preset (as expected — requirements files are internal SCP infra, not adopter-facing). However, the CODEOWNERS file does NOT include a `requirements/**` rule. Given that `requirements/policy-check.txt` is the new cryptographic root-of-trust for Python supply-chain verification (analogous to `scripts/scp-policy-check.lock` for binary supply-chain), the absence of CODEOWNERS coverage on `requirements/**` is a forward-looking governance gap.
findings.recommendation: Add `requirements/** @jrnb2024` to CODEOWNERS before the `/CODEOWNERS` self-protection line (per the ORDERING INVARIANT). This closes the same supply-chain governance coverage gap that 020H.2 R1 SAFE-002 closed for `scripts/**`. Symmetric with `scripts/**` and `vendor/**` coverage. Filing this as a tracked-forward item (new TF) is acceptable if not addressed in this slice; however, given the slice is still open, adding one CODEOWNERS line is low-risk.
findings.rationale: The review package examination item (5) specifically asks whether CODEOWNERS should include requirements/**. Per the estate pattern (scripts/** and vendor/** are both covered because they hold the supply-chain lockfiles), requirements/** should be covered for the same reason — a PR mutating requirements/policy-check.txt without CODEOWNERS coverage could silently introduce hash-drift. In single-operator count=0 mode this is documentary; in multi-maintainer mode it becomes machine-enforced.

summary: Slice 020M is well-constructed and represents a clean PATCH-level supply-chain hardening. The primary TF closure (TF-020H3rg-002) is complete: all 5 pip install sites across both workflows are converted, the lockfile pair is committed, the D-038 decision row is complete and correctly classified, and the release notes are adopter-sufficient. Two MAJ findings require attention before or immediately after merge: (1) COMP-MAJ-001 — the STATUS.md TF-020H3-003 closure description says 'Both occurrences' when three lines were corrected, creating an ambiguous cold-read; (2) COMP-MAJ-002 — ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 (supply-chain posture disclosure) is not updated to reflect the new Python dependency hash-pinning, leaving a disclosure gap against v1.0.1. Neither finding blocks the core correctness of the slice, but both should be resolved before the close-out is considered complete. The MAJ-002 ADOPT-001 gap is the more significant of the two: §12.7.13 is the primary adopter-facing supply-chain disclosure document and shipping v1.0.1 without updating it creates a stale disclosure. Recommended remediation: either a fast-follow PR amending §12.7.13 before the v1.0.1 tag is published, or a new TF filed in STATUS.md with a clear deadline. The CODEOWNERS gap on requirements/** (COMP-nit-003) is a governance forward-looking issue that should be filed as a TF. Verdict: APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS — the two MAJ findings are documentation gaps, not functional defects; the slice can merge with a committed close-out action to resolve them before the tag is cut.
